text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.59% today, continuing a four-day climb that's recovered most of last week's losses. The bounce tracks with a broader lift in oil markets: US crude is holding above $89 per barrel, and the stock has climbed nearly $6 since November 6th as energy prices stabilized after their recent dip. The company was also mentioned in CNBC's "calls of the day" on November 11th, which may have drawn renewed investor attention to the sector.

The recovery sits against a mixed backdrop for oil demand. While heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year—a sign of real energy demand heading into winter—the IEA reported that Russian crude production is rebounding and global oil markets are shifting back into surplus. That's the kind of supply overhang that can cap upside for oil prices and energy stocks, even if near-term seasonal demand remains solid.
